scope_summary: Rank one compact locally symmetric spaces Gamma backslash G/K for the four families SO_0(n,1), SU(n,1), Sp(n,1), F_4(-20), at the exceptional spectral parameters (zeros of the Harish-Chandra e-function). The paper characterizes the image of a vector valued (minimal K-type) Poisson transform on the socle and deduces an isomorphism between Gamma-invariant distribution vectors of the reducible spherical principal series and Gamma-invariant solutions of explicit generalized-gradient systems.

necessary_conditions.condition: G is a non-compact connected real semisimple Lie group with finite center; in the spectral correspondence G has real rank one and is one of SO_0(n,1), SU(n,1), Sp(n,1), F_4(-20).
Gamma <= G is a co-compact lattice; in Sections 5-6 and in all spectral statements Gamma is additionally torsion free. Section 4 explicitly does not assume torsion freeness (line 724).

mu lies in a*, and for the correspondence mu is exceptional: e(mu)=0, equivalently mu(H) in -(1/2)m_alpha-1-2N0 or -(1/2)m_alpha-m_{2alpha}-2N0 for the unique simple positive restricted root alpha with alpha(H)=1.

The minimal K-type is the one listed in the socle table: Y_{ell+1} for SO, Y_{ell+1,ell+1} for SU, V_{ell+1,ell+1} for Sp, V_{2ell+2,0} for F_4. The Poisson transform used is the vector valued one attached to THAT K-type, not the scalar Poisson transform.

The statement that Gamma-invariant distribution vectors lie in the socle requires the socle of the spherical principal series to decompose multiplicity-freely; in rank one this is supplied by a citation (C85), not reproved.
The Fourier characterization requires the distribution to be written as its full K-type Fourier expansion with every projected piece smooth; it is not a statement about arbitrary distributions.

quantifiers_and_regularity.literal: G non-compact, connected, real, semisimple, finite center; Gamma co-compact, torsion free (except Section 4). The correspondences are for the given fixed Gamma; there is no uniformity in Gamma and no statement about non-uniform lattices.

mu in a* arbitrary in Theorems 4.1 and 5.30; mu restricted to Ex = {mu_ell : ell in N0} in Theorems 4.5-4.7 and 6.1, 6.4, 6.6, 6.8, 6.10. The parameter is the Harish-Chandra parameter normalized as in GHWb, with a^mu = e^{mu(log a)} and rho the half-sum of positive restricted roots with multiplicity.

Generic means e(mu) != 0, equivalently the scalar Poisson transform P_mu is a topological isomorphism; at e(mu)=0 the scalar P_mu is neither injective nor surjective (Definition 3.1, line 449). Irreducibility of H_mu is sufficient but not necessary for bijectivity of P_mu (line 469). The exceptional parameters treated here are exactly the e-zeros.

The quantum-classical object is the space Gamma H_mu^{-infinity} of Gamma-invariant distribution vectors of the spherical principal series, realized on D'(K/M) or as R(mu-rho) in D'(G/M). The image side consists of Gamma-invariant SMOOTH sections of a homogeneous vector bundle; the isomorphism is between distribution vectors and smooth invariant solutions. No identification of smooth vectors of H_mu with solutions is claimed.

Theorem 4.1 is an isomorphism of Gamma H_mu^{-infinity} with the direct sum over irreducible subrepresentations of the socle; it is not an exactness statement for the full composition series. Proposition 3.10 describes the kernel of P_mu^tau as the closure of the sum of invariant subspaces missing the K-type tau; Proposition 3.11 gives injectivity of a direct sum over one K-type per irreducible. Surjectivity onto the invariant solution space is proved only in Theorems 6.1, 6.4, 6.6, 6.8, 6.10, case by case.

P_mu^tau is normalized by t(1) := phi_V, which yields P_mu^tau(f)(g) = (1/dim V) pr_V(pi_mu(g)^{-1} f). Changing this normalization changes the scalar coefficients in all six/five conditions, so any formalization must keep this normalization.

quantifiers_and_regularity.item: Normalization of exceptional parameters and rho
quantifiers_and_regularity.literal: alpha(H)=1; rho(H) equals (n-1)/2 for SO, n for SU, 2n+1 for Sp, 11 for F_4; root multiplicities (m_alpha,m_{2alpha}) are (n-1,0), (2n-2,1), (4n-4,3), (8,7). These values are used for every explicit scalar in the conditions.

The growth condition is sup over g in G of |e^{-r d_{G/K}(eK,gK)} f(g)| < infinity for some r>=0 (moderate growth) and is used to pass from Harish-Chandra modules to distribution vectors; for Gamma-invariant sections the supremum reduces to a compact fundamental domain, so the growth condition becomes automatic (proof of Theorem 6.1, lines 1902-1906). The mechanism which removes the growth condition is this compactness argument, not a general regularity theorem.

For S=G the socle is tempered; it is a discrete series representation iff mu_ell(H) <= -rho(H), and a limit of discrete series iff mu_ell(H) > -rho(H), a case the author says occurs only for Sp(2,1) and F_4(-20). The paper does not treat the limit cases differently in the correspondence.

explicit_non_claims: No general-rank statement: rank one is essential for multiplicity one of K-types, for the socle tables, and for the tensor decompositions.

No replacement of isomorphism by surjection or injection: every correspondence is stated as an isomorphism onto a specified Gamma-invariant solution space; the scalar Poisson transform at exceptional parameters is explicitly not injective and not surjective.
No claim that all Gamma-invariant smooth sections are Poisson images; only the sections satisfying the listed conditions.
No claim that H_mu itself is irreducible at exceptional parameters; the socle is the locus of Gamma-invariant vectors.
No new proof of the cited classification theorems (JW, JW2, DGK88, F79, K83, M89, Olbrich, C85, GHWb); where a proof is included it is because a reference was not readily available (B.1-B.3).
No uniformity in the lattice Gamma, no non-uniform lattice, no cuspidal case, no higher rank, no statement about all spectral parameters simultaneously.
